appropriate: a seed-shaped body with a leaf sprout and two small dot eyes reads at once as a small, quiet friend named for a seed; Caregiver warmth, but nothing in the shape carries reading aloud
distinctive: a coral seed character with small low eyes sits apart from the category's big-eyed owls, monsters and blue tiles, though a teardrop-with-leaf silhouette is not wholly ownable
simple: one teardrop body, one leaf, two dots; drawable from memory in seconds
legible: 'Pip' in bold rounded sans reads cleanly in every lockup; at 16 px the seed silhouette holds but the eyes merge into a speck and the leaf thins
adaptable: black, reversed white-on-black, one-colour 64 and 32, coral app tile, yellow-on-brown nav and avatar all work; no motion logic shown
timeless: a flat character mark (a 'use' trend where warmth is the strategy) with a rounded geometric sans that leans slightly toward the saturated rounded consumer look
universal: mirrored reads clean, but rotated 90 turns the body and leaf into a fish or tadpole with a tail
clear: unsearched: seed and drop characters with a leaf sprout are common in kids' and eco brands, and 'Pip and Tim' and Pip School already use the name in children's reading
congruent: round body, coral at medium chroma, one asymmetric leaf and lean, eyes about a tenth of body width, front-vowel smallness all match; the bottom is rounded rather than the flat grounded edge the ladder asks for
system: horizontal lockups, reversed, icon tile, favicon tab, nav bars, avatar and card all derive cleanly with the 256 to 16 ladder drawn; no stacked lockup shown
